name: Grey Lady
description: 'Grey Lady' is a recurring archetype in British, North American, and broader anglophone ghost-lore: a female apparition dressed in grey, usually associated with a specific historic building and a tragic backstory.
full_description: The 'Grey Lady' is not a single ghost but a class name for dozens of female apparitions reported across the anglophone world, particularly in the United Kingdom and the United States. The Wikipedia disambiguation page 'The Grey Lady' lists Grey Lady ghost legends at, among other sites, Rufford Old Hall (Lancashire), the Theatre Royal, Bath, Fort St. Angelo (Birgu, Malta), Cumberland College (Dunedin, New Zealand), the old parsonage at Sims, North Dakota, the Dark Hedges (County Antrim), Gainsborough Old Hall (Lincolnshire), and Willard Library (Evansville, Indiana). Outside the disambiguation, the 'Grey Lady of Hampton Court Palace' is widely identified with Sybil Penn (d. 1562), nurse to Tudor royalty, whose haunting was reported after her tomb was disturbed during a church rebuilding in 1829, and the 'Grey Lady of Glamis' is associated with Janet Douglas, Lady Glamis (c. 1498–1537), executed at Edinburgh Castle in 1537. Grey Ladies are typically described as silent, melancholy, dressed in grey, silver, or pale period clothing, and connected to a story of love, betrayal, injustice, or tragic death; sceptics regard the figure as a generic folkloric template attached opportunistically to historic buildings.
regions: New England and the Midwest US
origin: Anglophone world, with concentrations in the British Isles and North America. The Wikipedia disambiguation page lists Grey Lady ghosts in England, Northern Ireland, Malta, New Zealand, and the United States.

etymology.origin: English. The label appears to consolidate in Victorian and Edwardian ghost-story collecting, when many British country houses, theatres, and castles acquired named resident ghosts.
etymology.meaning: A female apparition habitually seen in grey or silvery clothing.

timeline.event: Janet Douglas, Lady Glamis, is executed by burning at Edinburgh Castle
timeline.significance: Historical anchor of the 'Grey Lady of Glamis' legend

timeline.event: Sybil Penn, Tudor royal nurse, dies in a smallpox outbreak
timeline.significance: Historical anchor of the 'Grey Lady of Hampton Court' legend

timeline.event: Sybil Penn's monument is disturbed during the rebuilding of St Mary's Hampton; spinning-wheel sounds and apparitions are subsequently reported at Hampton Court Palace
timeline.significance: Recognised origin of the modern Grey Lady haunting at Hampton Court

timeline.event: First widely-cited Willard Library Grey Lady sighting by a night custodian
timeline.significance: Earliest record of one of the most popular American Grey Lady cases

related.name: White Lady
related.description: Closely related female-apparition archetype; often more strongly associated with romantic tragedy

related.name: Banshee
related.description: Irish female apparition; herald of death rather than place-bound resident

cultural_notes: Grey Ladies are typically held to be the souls of historical women bound to their former residences by tragic injustice or unresolved grief.
